hints: Determine the normal reaction force $R$ perpendicular to the plane by balancing the component of weight: $R = 12g \cos \alpha$, where $\tan \alpha = 0.5 \implies \cos \alpha = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $\sin \alpha = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$.
As the block moves down the plane, the friction force acts up the plane with magnitude $F = \mu R = 0.15 R$.
Apply Newton's second law parallel to the incline ($12g \sin \alpha - X - F = 12a$) to solve for the acceleration $a$, then use $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find $t$.
walkthrough:
Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane to find the normal reaction $R$:
$$R = 12g \cos \alpha = 12 \times 10 \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}}\text{ N} \approx 107.33\text{ N}$$

Calculate the friction force $F = \mu R$ acting up the plane opposing downward motion, with $\mu = 0.15$:
$$F = 0.15 \times \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{36}{\sqrt{5}}\text{ N} \approx 16.10\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law down the plane ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) with $X = 20\text{ N}$ acting up the plane:
$$12g \sin \alpha - X - F = 12a$$
$$\frac{120}{\sqrt{5}} - 20 - \frac{36}{\sqrt{5}} = 12a$$
$$\frac{84}{\sqrt{5}} - 20 = 12a \implies 37.566 - 20 = 17.566 = 12a$$
$$a = \frac{17.566}{12} \approx 1.4638\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ from rest ($u = 0$) for distance $s = 2\text{ m}$:
$$2 = \frac{1}{2}(1.4638)t^2$$
$$t^2 = \frac{4}{1.4638} \approx 2.7326 \implies t = \sqrt{2.7326} \approx 1.65\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Begin by using the given trigonometric relation $\tan \alpha = 0.5 = \frac{1}{2}$. By constructing a right-angled triangle with opposite side $1$ and adjacent side $2$, the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{1^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{5}$:
$$\sin \alpha = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \approx 0.4472, \quad \cos \alpha = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \approx 0.8944$$

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane. The block does not lift off the plane, so the normal reaction $R$ balances the perpendicular component of the block's weight:
$$R = mg \cos \alpha$$
$$R = 12 \times 10 \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}} \approx 107.331\text{ N}$$

Because the block accelerates down the plane, friction opposes this motion and acts directly up the plane. Since motion takes place, friction is at its maximum limiting value:
$$F = \mu R$$
$$F = 0.15 \times \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{36}{\sqrt{5}} \approx 16.0997\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = ma$) parallel to the plane in the downward direction. The forces acting down the plane are the component of gravity down the incline ($mg \sin \alpha$), opposed by the applied upward force ($X = 20\text{ N}$) and the friction force ($F$):
$$mg \sin \alpha - X - F = ma$$
$$12(10)\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right) - 20 - \frac{36}{\sqrt{5}} = 12a$$
$$\frac{120 - 36}{\sqrt{5}} - 20 = 12a$$
$$\frac{84}{\sqrt{5}} - 20 = 12a$$

Evaluate the numerical value of the net force and solve for acceleration $a$:
$$\frac{84}{2.23607} - 20 = 37.5660 - 20 = 17.5660\text{ N}$$
$$12a = 17.5660$$
$$a = \frac{17.5660}{12} = 1.46383\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.46\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Now apply the constant acceleration formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to find the time required to travel $s = 2\text{ m}$ from rest ($u = 0$):
$$s = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$$
$$2 = \frac{1}{2}(1.46383) t^2$$
$$2 = 0.73192 t^2$$
$$t^2 = \frac{2}{0.73192} \approx 2.73255$$
$$t = \sqrt{2.73255} \approx 1.653\text{ s} \approx 1.65\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Resolves perpendicular to find $R = 12g \cos \alpha$, calculates $F = 0.15R$, applies N2L down the slope to find $a = 1.46\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and solves $2 = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to obtain $t = 1.65\text{ s}$.

hints: When the block is on the point of moving down the plane, limiting friction $F = \mu R$ acts up the plane.
Set up the equilibrium equation parallel to the plane for impending downward motion ($X_1 + F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$ with $X_1 = 10$) to find $F$ and $\mu = \frac{F}{R}$.
For impending upward motion, limiting friction $F$ acts down the plane; set up $X_2 - F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$ to solve for $X_2$.
walkthrough:
For impending motion down the plane with $X = 10\text{ N}$, friction $F$ acts up the plane:
$$10 + F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$$
$$F = 120 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} - 10 = \frac{120}{\sqrt{5}} - 10 \approx 53.666 - 10 = 43.666\text{ N} \approx 43.7\text{ N}$$

Use $F = \mu R$ with $R = \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}}\text{ N} \approx 107.33\text{ N}$ to find $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{\frac{120}{\sqrt{5}} - 10}{\frac{240}{\sqrt{5}}} = \frac{120 - 10\sqrt{5}}{240} = \frac{12 - \sqrt{5}}{24} \approx 0.4068 \approx 0.407$$

When the block is on the point of moving up the plane, friction $F$ acts down the plane:
$$X - F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$$
$$X = F + 12g \sin \alpha$$
$$X = 43.666 + 53.666 = 97.332\text{ N} \approx 97.3\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Recall that the normal reaction force remains unchanged:
$$R = 12g \cos \alpha = 120 \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{240}{\sqrt{5}} \approx 107.331\text{ N}$$

Case 1 (Impending motion down the plane): When $X = 10\text{ N}$ acts up the plane, the block is on the verge of sliding downwards. Friction opposes impending motion, so the limiting friction force $F$ acts up the plane:
$$\Sigma F_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$X + F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$$
$$10 + F - 120 \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right) = 0$$
$$F = \frac{120}{\sqrt{5}} - 10 \approx 53.6656 - 10 = 43.6656\text{ N}$$

Calculate the coefficient of friction using the definition of limiting friction $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{43.6656}{107.331} \approx 0.40683 \approx 0.407$$

Case 2 (Impending motion up the plane): For the block to be on the point of moving up the plane, the applied force $X$ acts up the plane while friction $F$ acts down the plane to oppose upward motion. Because $\mu$ and $R$ are unchanged, the magnitude of the limiting friction is the same: $F = 43.6656\text{ N}$.

Set up the equilibrium equation parallel to the incline:
$$\Sigma F_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$X - F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$$
$$X = F + 12g \sin \alpha$$
$$X = 43.6656 + 53.6656 = 97.3312\text{ N} \approx 97.3\text{ N}$$
The required values are $\mu = 0.407$ and $X = 97.3\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.Using Limiting Equilibrium: Sets $10 + F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$ to find $F = 43.7\text{ N}$, calculates $\mu = F/R = 0.407$, and solves $X - F - 12g \sin \alpha = 0$ to obtain $X = 97.3\text{ N}$.
